   "source": [
    "# Wakefield under uncertainty\n",
    "\n",
    "> **Uncertainty quantification plugs into every analysis.** A run is deterministic until you add a `uq_config`; with it, the analysis is evaluated over a small Stroud-3 quadrature of the uncertain geometry and returns a distribution (mean, standard deviation). The same pattern works for eigenmode, tuning, wakefield, and optimisation.\n",
    "\n",
    "Here the analysis is the **wakefield / impedance** solve (ABCI). The figure of merit is the peak longitudinal impedance $|Z_\\parallel|$ in chosen frequency windows — a `ZL` objective, `[goal, 'ZL', [f0, f1, …]]`, whose windows are the consecutive pairs of the frequency list (GHz). With a `uq_config`, each window's peak comes back as a **mean ± standard deviation** over the perturbed geometries instead of a single number.\n",
    "\n",
    "> Needs the bundled `ABCI.exe` (Windows, or `wine` elsewhere). ABCI needs beam pipes at both ends, so the cavity is built with `beampipe='both'`. See the [wakefield guide](../../wakefield) and the deterministic [wakefield example](../wakefield/impedance.ipynb)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "eeaa7e59",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-26T08:20:42.934432Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-07-26T08:20:42.934312Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-07-26T08:20:44.548627Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-07-26T08:20:44.547712Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "import tempfile\n",
    "\n",
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "\n",
    "from cavsim2d import Study, EllipticalCavity\n",
    "from cavsim2d.utils.style import apply_style\n",
    "\n",
    "apply_style()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "8767b8dc",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 1. The cavity and the uncertainty\n",
    "\n",
    "A TESLA-like mid-cell in a one-cavity study (UQ perturbs the geometry, so it runs through `Study`, not a bare `Cavity`). The `uq_config` puts a **0.05 mm spread** on the ellipse semi-axes `A, B` (`delta` is an additive perturbation in mm) and asks for the `ZL` peaks in two windows: 0.2–2.0 GHz and 2.0–5.0 GHz."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "8790673e",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-26T08:20:44.551478Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-07-26T08:20:44.551102Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-07-26T08:20:44.562043Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-07-26T08:20:44.561286Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "cavs = Study(os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 'wake_uq'))\n",
    "midcell = [42, 42, 12, 19, 35, 57.7, 103.353]\n",
    "cavs.add_cavity([EllipticalCavity(1, midcell, midcell, midcell, beampipe='both')], ['W'])\n",
    "\n",
    "config = {\n",
    "    'MROT': 2, 'wakelength': 20, 'bunch_length': 25, 'processes': 1,\n",
    "    'uq_config': {\n",
    "        'variables': ['A', 'B'],\n",
    "        'objectives': [['min', 'ZL', [0.2, 2.0, 5.0]]],\n",
    "        'method': ['stroud3'], 'delta': [0.05, 0.05], 'processes': 1,\n",
    "        'cell_type': 'mid-cell', 'cell_complexity': 'simplecell',\n",
    "    },\n",
    "}"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "905b4cf4",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 2. Run it\n",
    "\n",
    "Every quadrature node is a full ABCI wakefield solve, so this is the slowest of the UQ examples — a handful of perturbed geometries, each a complete time-domain run."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "f222be4a",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-26T08:20:44.564696Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-07-26T08:20:44.564526Z",
     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-07-26T08:35:51.850238Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-07-26T08:35:51.849723Z"
    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "windows: ['ZL [max(0.2<f<2.0)]', 'ZL [max(2.0<f<5.0)]']\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "cavs.run_wakefield(config)\n",
    "uq = cavs.uq_hom_results['W']\n",
    "print('windows:', list(uq))"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "f0e235cd",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 3. The impedance spread\n",
    "\n",
    "For each frequency window the result carries the **mean** `expe` and **standard deviation** `stdDev` of the peak $|Z_\\parallel|$ across the perturbed geometries — the spread the tolerance band induces on the HOM impedance."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "e0646e1a",
   "metadata": {

    }

   ],
   "source": [
    "df = pd.DataFrame({\n",
    "    window: {'E[ZL] [Ohm]': v['expe'][0], 'std[ZL] [Ohm]': v['stdDev'][0]}\n",
    "    for window, v in uq.items()\n",
    "}).T\n",
    "df.round(2)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0a531d9d",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 4. Plot the mean with its uncertainty band"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "eb81f9a9",
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-26T08:35:51.862108Z",
     "iopub.status.busy": "2026-07-26T08:35:51.861972Z",

    }
   },
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 600x400 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))\n",
    "labels = list(uq)\n",
    "means = [uq[w]['expe'][0] for w in labels]\n",
    "stds = [uq[w]['stdDev'][0] for w in labels]\n",
    "ax.bar(range(len(labels)), means, yerr=stds, capsize=6)\n",
    "ax.set_xticks(range(len(labels)))\n",
    "ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=15, ha='right')\n",
    "ax.set_ylabel(r'peak $|Z_\\parallel|$  [$\\Omega$]')\n",
    "ax.set_title('Longitudinal impedance under a 0.05 mm A/B tolerance')\n",
    "fig.tight_layout()\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
